structured.approach: Loaded the backend-steps skill for BE-01. Read both contracted inputs (feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack) to find the repository the Backend tasks need: ap_aging for TSK-05 and TSK-06. This step does not allow shell commands (the G9 hook blocked them), so I used the step's tool view as the evidence for availability, branch and write access. I backed it up by reading repository files directly: .git/HEAD, CLAUDE.md, ci.py, src/ap_aging/__init__.py and a file listing. No connector was needed because the inputs held every fact. I wrote task.repo_access with the result, the repository facts later steps rely on, assumptions, and two non-blocking open questions.

claims.text: The Backend lane's tasks TSK-05 (STORY-05) and TSK-06 (STORY-06) both target the ap_aging repository.
Repository ap_aging is available locally, so it does not need to be created.
The agent identity has write access to ap_aging, and git status is clean.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at 5d2cbb9, and HEAD points to refs/heads/feature/story.
No Databricks, database or other workspace is used by ap_aging.
The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py. It enforces line coverage of at least 90% (COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0) plus static checks that stand in for SonarQube, including lines of at most 140 characters.
The current ap_aging version is 1.4.0, the only export is aging_buckets, and TSK-05 owns the version step.
ci.py imports the third-party coverage package, while the repository is described as Python 3.9 standard library.
Commit messages must start with the story ID; the task ID may follow.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): Is the coverage package installed for /usr/bin/python3 where ap_aging's ci.py runs? Interim answer: assume yes; the first CI run in BE-05/BE-06 will show it. Owner: infra team.

RAQ-2 (non-blocking): Should TSK-05 and TSK-06 share the provided branch feature/story, or use one branch per story (feature/STORY-05, feature/STORY-06)? Interim answer: share feature/story; commits carry the story ID. Owner: Developer.
structured.summary: ap_aging, the only repository the Backend tasks need (TSK-05 and TSK-06), is available locally with write access. It is on branch feature/story, created from dev at 5d2cbb9. No repository has to be created and no Databricks or other workspace is needed. task.repo_access records this, along with the CI gate (at least 90% coverage plus static checks), the current version 1.4.0 and the files in budget. Two non-blocking questions remain: whether the coverage package is installed for the CI, and whether both stories should share the branch name.

tool_input.command: git status --short --branch && git branch -a -vv && git remote -v && git log --oneline -3 && ls && ls src/ap_aging tests && cat src/ap_aging/__init__.py && test -w . && test -w .git && echo WRITABLE
tool_input.description: Inspect ap_aging repo branches, remotes, layout and write permission

tool_input.command: git -C ap-aging-sample status --short --branch; git -C ap-aging-sample branch -a -vv; git -C ap-aging-sample log --oneline -3
tool_input.description: Show ap_aging branch status and recent commits
